samples.summary: An empty batch now pops a checkpoint it did not push (the adopted `snapshot()` one), stranding writes that follow it in the same action
samples.evidence: `batch()` may now adopt the top-of-stack checkpoint (`memory.ts:222-226`) but the `wroteNothing` branch still `this.undoStack.pop()`s unconditionally (`memory.ts:251-254`). Out-of-diff callers rely on `saveSnapshot()` → `deleteSelection()` (which opens its own unit) → *more writes outside any unit*: `packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2500-2508` (handleBackspace), `:2551-2560` (handleDelete), `:2600-2607` (handleWordBackspace), `:2621-2630` (handleWordDelete), `:3425-3431` (handleLineBackspace). `deleteSelectionImpl` can return **false without writing** after its batch is open — `text-editor.ts:3942` (`getNormalizedRange` returns null when a selection endpoint's block is not in the layout, see `selection.ts:118`/`150`) and `text-editor.ts:3948` (`tableCellRange` whose block has no `tableData`). In that case the adopted checkpoint the preceding `saveSnapshot()` pushed is popped, the handler falls through and deletes a character with **no checkpoint on the stack**, so on `MemDocStore` (slides text boxes / table cells, the docs demo, the visual harness) that keystroke is either not undoable at all or the next Cmd+Z reverts the previous action too. Before this delta `batch()` pushed and popped its *own* clone, so the snapshot's checkpoint survived. Fix belongs on the new code: only pop when `!adopted`.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. memory.ts:220-226 adopts the top-of-stack checkpoint pushed by a preceding snapshot() (memory.ts:177-184) instead of pushing its own, but the finally block's wroteNothing branch still pops unconditionally (memory.ts:248-254) — with `before === top` the identity test holds, so an empty batch removes a checkpoint it never pushed. Out-of-diff callers depend on the old behaviour: saveSnapshot is `() => docStore.snapshot()` (text-box-editor.ts:680; same wiring for editor.ts:2455), deleteSelection() opens a unit whenever hasSelection() is true (text-editor.ts:3859-3866), and deleteSelectionImpl can return false without writing at text-editor.ts:3942 and :3948 — reachable because normalizeRange returns null for endpoints not in layout (selection.ts:152) and for mixed/cross-cell selections (selection.ts:171). The handlers then write outside any unit (text-editor.ts:2500-2508, 2551-2560, 2600-2601, 2621-2622, 3425-3426), so that keystroke lands with no checkpoint on the MemDocStore undo stack. No guard prevents the write-free batch. In-lane (changed contract, unupdated consumers) and major.

finding.summary: `saveSnapshot()` before `withUndoUnit()` costs a dead Cmd+Z on every MemDocStore-backed host (slides text boxes, docs demo, hunt/visual harness)
finding.evidence: `withUndoUnit` documents (text-editor.ts:3807) that `saveSnapshot()` must run *before* the unit opens. On `YorkieDocStore` `snapshot()` is a no-op, so that is free — but `MemDocStore.snapshot()` pushes an undo checkpoint (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:181-183) and `MemDocStore.batch()` then pushes a *second, identical* checkpoint up front (memory.ts:206-209), keeping it because the body wrote (memory.ts:230-236). The repo already documents exactly this hazard and takes the opposite ordering for it: packages/docs/src/view/link-run.ts:81-85 — "`MemDocStore.batch()` takes its own checkpoint up front, so a call before the batch costs a second, identical undo step (a dead Cmd+Z) and clears the redo stack that `batch()` puts back" — and `withNamedStyleChange` puts `docStore.snapshot()` *inside* the batch (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1238-1239). Affected out-of-diff consumers: packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:431/680/682 (Slides text boxes and Slides table cells run `TextEditor` over a `MemDocStore` with `saveSnapshot = docStore.snapshot()` and `undo = docStore.undo()`), packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1042 (default store when no store is passed: demo.ts, harness scenarios, revision-preview). Because `handleInput` wraps unconditionally (text-editor.ts:995-1001), *every* keystroke — not just selection-replacing ones — now leaves two identical undo entries there, so undo needs two presses per edit and the first-of-two looks like it did nothing. Existing docs tests only ever press undo once (e.g. packages/docs/test/view/copy-integrity.test.ts:790), so nothing catches it. Fix belongs on the new code: either call `saveSnapshot()` inside the unit (as link-run/withNamedStyleChange do) or have `withUndoUnit` take the snapshot itself.

verdict.reason: The finding's core mechanism is not what the code does. It claims MemDocStore.batch() pushes a second, identical checkpoint when saveSnapshot() ran immediately before it. In fact batch() explicitly adopts such a checkpoint: memory.ts:220-227 computes `adopted = top !== undefined && JSON.stringify(top) === beforeJson` and only pushes when `!adopted`, so no second undo entry is created. The comment at memory.ts:206-219 names this exact scenario ("pushing a second, identical one would cost a dead Cmd+Z on every edit in every MemDocStore host (slides text boxes, the docs demo, the visual harness)") and is the guard's rationale, not evidence of the bug. The claim that "nothing catches it" is also false: test/store/memory.test.ts:317-337 pins it — snapshot() then batch(), one undo restores the pre-edit text and canUndo() is false, i.e. no dead second press; :339-345 and :347-356 cover the empty-batch and write-between-snapshot-and-batch cases. The link-run.ts precedent is misquoted: link-run.ts:86-89 actually states that TextEditor.withUndoUnit() must snapshot *before* its batch and that MemDocStore.batch() adopts an identical prior checkpoint rather than doubling it. Checking the named out-of-diff consumer: text-box-editor.ts:431 uses a plain MemDocStore, and text-editor.ts:1013 calls saveSnapshot() with no intervening store write before withUndoUnit() (text-editor.ts:3839-3842) opens the batch at :1019 — precisely the adopted===true path. So the alleged double undo entry is unreachable on the cited path.
